q: You must fetch a vendor name using vendor code, but the code column sits to the RIGHT of the name column in the master. Best single approach in Excel 2016 without restructuring the data?
o: VLOOKUP with a negative column index number to look leftward
INDEX on the name column with MATCH on the vendor code column
HLOOKUP with the range lookup argument set to FALSE for exact
VLOOKUP after sorting the master ascending by the vendor code
why: VLOOKUP can only return values to the right of the lookup column and a negative index simply errors, whereas INDEX with MATCH lets the return column sit anywhere. Sorting does not change the direction limitation.

q: A formula in D2 reads =B2*$F$1 and is copied to D3 and to E2. What happens to the $F$1 reference?
o: It stays $F$1 in both copies, since column and row are locked
It becomes $F$2 in D3 and $G$1 in E2 once the formula is copied
It becomes $F$2 in D3 but stays $F$1 in the copy made to E2
It becomes $G$1 in E2 but stays $F$1 in the copy made to D3
why: A dollar before the column letter locks the column and a dollar before the row number locks the row, making $F$1 fully absolute so it never shifts on copy. Only the relative B2 portion adjusts.

q: You need the total of the Amount column where Branch equals Pune AND the Date falls in Q3. Which is the correct function choice?
o: SUMIF with the two criteria separated by a comma in one call
DSUM with a criteria range, the only multi condition sum tool
SUMIFS, where the sum range comes first, then criteria pairs
SUMPRODUCT, the only function able to take two conditions here
why: SUMIFS supports multiple criteria and uniquely takes the sum range as its FIRST argument, unlike SUMIF where the sum range comes last. SUMIF accepts only one condition and SUMPRODUCT, while workable, is not the intended tool.

q: XLOOKUP is available in your version of Excel. Which statement about it is accurate?
o: XLOOKUP defaults to approximate match in the same way VLOOKUP does
XLOOKUP cannot search a list upward from the bottom of a range
XLOOKUP needs the lookup array and return array to be adjacent
XLOOKUP defaults to exact match and takes an if not found value
why: XLOOKUP defaults to exact match, unlike VLOOKUP whose fourth argument defaults to approximate, and its if_not_found argument removes the need to wrap it in IFERROR. It also supports reverse search and non adjacent arrays.

q: A debtors ageing pivot was built on a 60000 row extract. The client sends 3000 extra rows appended below and the pivot still shows old totals after Refresh. Most likely cause?
o: The pivot cache is corrupt, so the workbook must be rebuilt now
The source is a fixed range, so appended rows fall outside it
Pivot tables cannot handle populations larger than 60000 rows
Refresh updates only calculated fields and not the underlying data
why: A pivot built on a fixed cell range never extends to appended rows, so converting the source to an Excel Table or dynamic named range fixes it permanently. Refresh does rebuild from source, so the definition of the source is the problem.

q: What is the key difference between Remove Duplicates and the UNIQUE function when deduplicating a customer list in a workpaper?
o: Remove Duplicates is case sensitive while UNIQUE is not at all
UNIQUE works on one column only while Remove Duplicates handles many
Remove Duplicates deletes source rows while UNIQUE spills a result
There is no functional difference beyond the Excel version used
why: Remove Duplicates is destructive and irreversible once saved, which is a serious problem for audit evidence, while UNIQUE returns a live array and preserves the auditable population. Both are case insensitive and both can operate across multiple columns.

q: A bank statement download shows dates as text like 05/04/2026 in DD/MM/YYYY and SUMIFS by month returns zero. Which conversion approach is most reliable?
o: Use Text to Columns with the column data format set to Date DMY
Format the cells as Date using the Format Cells dialog box now
Apply the VALUE function directly to each of the text entries
Widen the column so that Excel recognises the entries as real dates
why: Formatting cells only changes display and does not convert text into a date serial, while Text to Columns with an explicit DMY setting parses correctly and prevents day and month being swapped. VALUE follows the system locale and can silently misread DD/MM as MM/DD.

q: Which use of IFERROR in an audit workpaper is a legitimate review point of concern?
o: Wrapping a VLOOKUP so unmatched items show blank not an error
Using IFERROR on a division to suppress a divide by zero error
Using IFERROR on a presentation tab rather than in the workings
Wrapping a whole reconciliation so any error returns a zero
why: Suppressing every error to zero hides genuine broken references and makes a reconciliation appear to tie when it does not, defeating the control purpose of the schedule. Targeted use for expected non matches or zero denominators is acceptable if disclosed.

q: You are reconciling a client sales ledger to a warehouse despatch listing, each about 40000 rows, matched on invoice number. Which technique isolates ALL differences?
o: A single VLOOKUP from the sales ledger into the despatch listing file
Look up both ways, review non matches and compare matched values
Sort both listings by amount and compare the two sets visually
Use conditional formatting to highlight duplicates across both
why: A one directional lookup finds items missing from the second list but silently misses items present only in that second list, so a two way match is essential. Matched keys can still carry different values, making the amount comparison a necessary third step.

q: To detect missing invoice numbers in a sequence like INV-2025-00001 upward, which approach is MOST reliable?
o: Sort ascending and scan visually for any break in the number series
Use COUNTIF and compare the total with the client stated count
Extract the number, sort it and flag gaps against the prior row
Run Remove Duplicates and check whether the row count falls off
why: Comparing consecutive extracted values mathematically catches every gap, including a single missing number, and also flags duplicates as a zero difference. A total count comparison can agree coincidentally when a gap is offset by a duplicate.

q: A senior reviewing your depreciation workpaper objects that the rate of 6.33 percent is typed directly into every formula. Why is this the strongest objection?
o: It cannot be traced to source and cannot be updated in one place
Typed constants slow Excel recalculation across the whole workbook
Percentages must always be entered as decimals inside formulas
Hardcoded values do not print correctly in a finalised workpaper
why: A hardcoded constant is invisible to a reviewer tracing precedents, needs editing in many cells if it changes and severs the link to the underlying source evidence. Objections about speed or printing are irrelevant to review quality.

q: Which combination gives the most meaningful integrity control over a shared audit schedule?
o: Password protect the file so that only the preparer can open it
Save the file as a PDF after every change has been made to it
Hide the formula sheet so that reviewers see only the outputs
Lock the formula cells, leave inputs open and add a check row
why: Cell level protection stops accidental overwriting of logic while still permitting data entry, and a self checking control total gives immediate visible assurance the schedule ties. Hiding sheets or converting to PDF removes reviewability instead of adding control.

q: COUNTIFS is used as =COUNTIFS(B:B,>1000000,C:C,Approved) and the count differs from a manual filter count. Which is the most likely legitimate cause?
o: COUNTIFS always excludes the first row of the specified range
COUNTIFS skips numbers stored as text that the filter still shows
COUNTIFS cannot handle more than one criterion in a single call
Filters count the hidden rows in the total whereas COUNTIFS does not
why: Numeric criteria in COUNTIFS do not match values stored as text, understating the count against what is visible in a filter. COUNTIFS does include hidden rows, so the hidden row explanation is the wrong way round.

q: For a monetary unit sampling selection from a 25000 line revenue population, which Excel approach is most defensible in the workpaper?
o: Use RAND to pick rows and record only the selected line numbers here
Sort descending by value and take items from the top until coverage is fair
Build a cumulative column, set the interval and log the random start
Use the Data Analysis Toolpak random generator on its default settings
why: MUS needs a cumulative value column, a stated sampling interval and a reproducible random start, with the derivation documented so a reviewer can re-perform the selection. RAND is volatile and recalculates, destroying reproducibility unless values are pasted and documented.

q: Your ageing pivot summarises the Amount field as Count instead of Sum for some months. What is the most likely cause in the underlying data?
o: The Amount column holds blanks or text, so it is not numeric
The pivot has too many rows for Excel to sum the values reliably
Pivot tables default to Count for any field formatted as currency
The Amount column is formatted as Accounting and not as Number
why: Excel defaults a pivot value field to Count whenever the source column contains any non numeric entry such as text or a stray label. Number formatting has no influence on the default aggregation.

q: Which statement about VLOOKUP with the fourth argument omitted is correct and most dangerous in audit work?
o: It matches exactly and returns not available when nothing matches
It returns a zero value whenever no matching value can be found
It sorts the lookup table automatically before matching the value
It defaults to approximate match and can return a wrong value
why: Omitting the range lookup argument makes VLOOKUP approximate, and on unsorted data it returns a plausible neighbouring value with no error signal at all. A silent wrong answer in a workpaper is far more damaging than a visible error.

q: You must compare two trial balances whose account codes differ in format, one text with leading zeros and one numeric. What is the safest first step?
o: Delete the leading zeros from the text version so both agree
Build a documented helper key on both sides using TEXT or TRIM
Use an approximate match lookup so that near matches are captured
Change the numeric column to text through cell formatting only
why: A documented helper key preserves both original populations while making the join reliable, keeping the evidence auditable. Stripping leading zeros destroys the original code and cell formatting alone does not change the underlying value type.

q: A pivot table shows total sales of Rs 84.2 crore while the underlying SUM shows Rs 86.9 crore. Which check is most likely to explain the difference?
o: Check whether the value field needs currency formatting applied
Check whether the source data spans more than one worksheet tab
Check for a filter or slicer and whether the source range is short
Check whether the pivot uses Average, which understates a total
why: An applied filter or slicer and a source range stopping short of the last data row are the two usual reasons a pivot total falls below the raw sum. Formatting cannot change totals, and an Average would give a wildly different figure rather than a small shortfall.
